c.tagline: Java's easternmost frontier -- blue-fire volcano, wild safari plains and the ferry to Bali.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis are scarce; use the Gojek or Grab apps, or agree a fare before an ojek (motorbike) or private-car ride, especially for pre-dawn trips up to Ijen.

emergency.note: 112 works as a general emergency line; 110 reaches police and 118/119 the ambulance service.

avoid.reason: Beware unofficial guides and inflated fees around Kawah Ijen tours; in town only usual awareness is needed.

hood_desc: The walkable core around the Taman Blambangan and Sri Tanjung squares, where the Saturday night market and Gandrung dance events take place; close to the market, the grand mosque and most in-town hotels -- the easiest base.

Banyuwangi's seafront on the Bali Strait, anchored by Pantai Boom beach, the open-air festival amphitheatre and the Gandrung Terakota statue field; a breezy spot for sunrise over Bali, seafood warungs and the city's big festivals.

The harbour district in the north where round-the-clock ferries cross to Gilimanuk on Bali in about 45 minutes; a practical transit zone of budget losmen and tour hotels used by travellers heading up to the Ijen crater before dawn.

A hilly coastal strip north of town climbing toward Watudodol, with clifftop sea views over the strait, small beaches and quiet fishing hamlets; calm and scenic, better for a relaxed stay than for nightlife.

Banyuwangi's historic quarter, mixing a Chinese temple (klenteng), an Arab-Indonesian trading community and the colonial-era 'Inggrisan' telegraph building where the undersea cable once ran to Australia; a low-key area of heritage and street food.

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water only.

transit.hours: Angkots run mainly in daylight, roughly 6:00 AM to early evening; the Ketapang-Gilimanuk ferry and ride-hailing operate around the clock.
transit.note: Getting around relies on angkot minibuses, Trans Jatim regional buses and ride-hailing (Gojek/Grab). The town's defining transport link is the 24-hour car ferry from Ketapang to Gilimanuk on Bali, about 45 minutes across the Bali Strait.
transit.pay: Angkot and local-bus fares are a low flat cash rate; the Ketapang-Gilimanuk ferry is a cheap fixed ticket. Gojek and Grab apps are the simplest way around town and accept cash or e-wallets.

ferry: Ketapang Ferry Port (ASDP crossings to Gilimanuk, Bali, roughly every 30-60 min, 24/7)
train: Ketapang Station; intercity trains to Surabaya, Malang and Jember

transit.m: Gojek/Grab or airport taxi to the town center (~20-30 min)
Angkot/Damri connection toward Rogojampi and the town

tip.r: Not expected; rounding up or leaving small change for good service is appreciated. Ijen guides and drivers are commonly tipped a small amount.

food.name: Rujak Soto
food.desc: Banyuwangi's famous collision of two dishes: a peanut-and-shrimp-paste vegetable rujak drowned in beef soto broth with offal, lontong and crackers.

places.name: Rujak Soto Mbok Mbret
places.note: The name locals give first; decades-old warung that made rujak soto famous beyond the regency

places.name: Pondok Rujak Soto
places.note: Long-running legendary spot pairing rujak with rich beef soto broth

places.name: Rujak Soto Mbok Nah
places.note: Same family kitchen as the celebrated sego tempong; busy from mid-morning

food.name: Sego Tempong
food.desc: "Slap rice": hot rice with blanched greens, tempe, tofu, fried fish or chicken and a raw chilli sambal fierce enough to feel like a smack.

places.name: Sego Tempong Mbok Nah
places.note: Open since the 1990s; crisp-fried egg and cheap plates make it the benchmark version

places.name: Sego Tempong Mbok Wah
places.note: Perpetually packed warung, another of the town's two great tempong institutions

places.name: Sego Tempong Mbah Wit
places.note: Late-opening favourite for a very raw, very hot sambal

food.name: Pecel Pitik
food.desc: Osing ceremonial dish of free-range chicken grilled over coals, torn by hand and dressed in young grated coconut with chilli and kencur.

places.name: Sanggar Genjah Arum
places.note: Osing cultural compound in traditional houses; pecel pitik served with village coffee

places.name: Pesantogan Kemangi
places.note: Riverside Osing eatery specialising in Kemiren home cooking for visitors

places.name: Warung Osing Kemiren
places.note: Simple village kitchens along the Kemiren main road cooking the dish to order

food.name: Ayam Kesrut
food.desc: Osing chicken soup made sour and searing with bird's-eye chilli, shallots and belimbing wuluh; a thin broth that clears the head instantly.

places.name: Pesantogan Kemangi
places.note: Reliable place to find kesrut on a normal day rather than only at ceremonies

places.name: Sanggar Genjah Arum
places.note: Serves the Osing repertoire including kesrut alongside pecel pitik

places.name: Warung-warung Desa Kemiren
places.note: Village warungs where the sour-chilli broth is a daily household staple

food.name: Sego Cawuk
food.desc: The local breakfast: rice topped with grated coconut and young-corn broth, dried fish, pindang and egg, eaten before the market gets going.

places.name: Sego Cawuk Bu Mantih
places.note: Long-established morning warung; sells out well before midday

places.name: Pasar Banyuwangi morning stalls
places.note: Cluster of breakfast vendors ladling cawuk broth from dawn

places.name: Sego Cawuk Bu Ning
places.note: Neighbourhood breakfast spot with the classic coconut-and-corn topping

food.name: Pindang Koyong
food.desc: Turmeric-yellow sour fish soup from the coast, made with tuna or mackerel, lemongrass, tomato and belimbing wuluh; Muncar's fishing-port dish.

places.name: Warung seafood Pelabuhan Muncar
places.note: Port-side kitchens cooking whatever the fleet landed that morning

places.name: Pantai Cacalan food stalls
places.note: Beachfront warungs with grilled fish and pindang koyong at sunrise

places.name: Pujasera Taman Blambangan
places.note: Evening food court gathering many Banyuwangi specialities in one place

food.name: Kopi Osing Kemiren
food.desc: Robusta grown on Ijen's slopes, roasted in village pans and brewed thick and sweet in a glass; served with the grounds still settling.

places.name: Sanggar Genjah Arum
places.note: Coffee roasted and ground in front of guests as part of the Osing house tour

places.name: Pesantogan Kemangi
places.note: Village coffee alongside Osing snacks in a bamboo riverside setting

places.name: Warung kopi around Taman Blambangan
places.note: Everyday coffee stalls where locals drink the same Ijen robusta

food.name: Es Temulawak
food.desc: Iced jamu-style cooler of wild ginger with tamarind, palm sugar and lime; bitter-sweet, faintly medicinal and sold on every hot afternoon.

places.name: Pasar Banyuwangi jamu sellers

places.name: Warung along Jl. Kolonel Sugiono

landmarks: Kawah Ijen (Ijen Crater)
A pre-dawn hike reveals electric-blue sulfur flames and the world's largest acidic crater lake, glowing turquoise inside this legendary volcano.
De Djawatan Forest
An enchanting grove of giant, fern-draped trembesi trees resembling Lord of the Rings' Fangorn Forest, a photographer's dream.
Alas Purwo National Park and G-Land
Java's oldest sacred forest hides ancient temples, grazing banteng, and Plengkung Beach's world-famous G-Land surf break.
Kemiren Osing Village
The cultural heartland of the indigenous Osing people, alive with gandrung dance, traditional coffee rituals, and distinctive wooden houses.
Bangsring Underwater
A community-run marine conservation zone in the Bali Strait with snorkeling over restored coral gardens and a floating house reef.
Sukamade Turtle Beach
Deep in Meru Betiri National Park, rangers guide nighttime vigils as giant sea turtles haul ashore to lay eggs.
Grand Watu Dodol Beach
A black-sand shoreline marked by a giant offshore boulder and gandrung dancer statue, gazing across the strait to Bali.
Tabuhan Island
An uninhabited islet of white sand and steady winds in the Bali Strait, a haven for kitesurfing and vibrant snorkeling.
Taman Blambangan
The green heart of Banyuwangi, a shaded central park with walking paths and open lawns that hosts the city's festivals and everyday gatherings.
Pantai Boom (Boom Beach)
A lively urban beach on the city's eastern edge with a marina, amusement rides and an amphitheater, popular for sunrise views over the Bali Strait.

train.note: Kereta Api Indonesia trains run from Banyuwangi Kota and Ketapang stations west to Jember, Probolinggo, Malang and Surabaya, with connections onward to Yogyakarta. There are no international trains in Indonesia.

bus.note: Buses from Sri Tanjung terminal serve Surabaya, Jember and Bali (Denpasar) via the Ketapang-Gilimanuk ferry crossing. No scheduled international coaches operate.

intl.to: Gilimanuk, Bali (Indonesia) - from Ketapang harbour, ~45 min, every 30-60 min around the clock

ferry.note: The signature route is the ASDP car-and-passenger ferry from Ketapang harbour across the Bali Strait to Gilimanuk on Bali -- roughly a 45-minute crossing running 24 hours a day, every 30-60 minutes, and the main overland gateway between Java and Bali.

full.blurb: A pre-dawn trek to the electric-blue sulphur flames and turquoise acid crater lake -- Banyuwangi's signature trip.
full.name: Ijen Crater (Kawah Ijen)

full.blurb: The 'Africa of Java' -- savanna plains with wild deer, buffalo and peacocks, plus Bama beach, north of town.
full.name: Baluran National Park

full.blurb: A remote Meru Betiri turtle-nesting beach where green turtles come ashore at night, reached on an overnight 4x4 trip.
full.name: Sukamade Beach

half.blurb: A laid-back surf beach with a red-tinged islet you can walk to at low tide, about two hours southwest.
